title: YouTube Search Terms: See What Viewers Typed to Find You

scenes.vo: Your YouTube title is a guess. Your viewers already typed the right one. You just never looked.

lines.text: viewers already typed the right one.

scenes.vo: Open YouTube Studio. Go to Content, and pick an old video.
scenes.head: STEP 1 // find the report

scenes.vo: Click Analytics, then the Reach tab. Scroll to the card called YouTube search terms.
scenes.head: STEP 2 // the card nobody opens

scenes.vo: These are the exact words people typed before they found your video.
scenes.head: YouTube search terms  //  EXAMPLE DATA

scenes.vo: Now hold that list next to your title. If the top phrase isn't in it, there's your problem.
scenes.head: STEP 3 // compare

scenes.vo: Put that phrase near the start of the title. Only if the video really delivers it.
scenes.head: STEP 4 // fix

lines.text: Budget Camera for YouTube: My Setup
check: does the video deliver it?  yes

scenes.vo: Then use that same phrase in the first line of your description. Same words people search for.
scenes.head: STEP 5 // description

lines.text: line 1: "budget camera for youtube, my setup"
title and description match the search

scenes.vo: Card empty? That video barely gets search traffic yet. Start with one that does.
scenes.head: EDGE CASE

lines.text: skip it. start with a video that has some.

scenes.vo: Do this for five old videos this week. Change one thing at a time, so you know what worked.
